caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.

The figure presents a donut chart designed to display the distribution of samples across two dimensions: sample-level ambiguity standard deviation and sample-level maximum ambiguity. The chart consists of two concentric rings, with the outer ring representing the distribution of samples by ambiguity standard deviation and the inner ring representing the distribution by maximum ambiguity. 

The outer ring is divided into four slices: the largest slice, representing 49.0% of the samples, is colored the darkest blue and corresponds to a standard deviation of 0.0; the second-largest slice, accounting for 38.0% of the samples, is colored a lighter blue and corresponds to a standard deviation of 0.47; the third slice, representing 7.0% of the samples, is colored an even lighter blue and corresponds to a standard deviation of 0.82; and the smallest slice, accounting for 5.0% of the samples, is colored the lightest blue and corresponds to a standard deviation of 0.94. 

The inner ring is also divided into three slices: the largest slice, representing 47.7% of the samples, is colored the lightest blue and corresponds to a maximum ambiguity of 2; the second-largest slice, accounting for 39.0% of the samples, is colored a medium blue and corresponds to a maximum ambiguity of 1; and the smallest slice, representing 14.2% of the samples, is colored a darker blue and corresponds to a maximum ambiguity of 3. 

The chart includes a legend that provides a key to the colors used for each level of ambiguity standard deviation and maximum ambiguity. The slices in both rings are labeled with their corresponding percentages, but there are no percentage labels inside the slices. The slices in each ring appear to be ordered by their percentage values in descending order.

The chart includes a legend and labels each slice with its percentage value, but does not include percentage labels inside the slices; the slices in both rings appear to be ordered by their percentage values in descending order.
